items.name: The liquid-cooling transition
items.note: Blackwell rack systems are liquid-cooled by design; 120kW-class racks ended air cooling's run at the AI high end

items.name: PUE and efficiency reporting
items.note: Google publishes fleet-wide power usage effectiveness (trailing twelve-month ~1.1) as the reference efficiency disclosure

reading.body:
US datacenters already consume 4.4% of national electricity, and the DOE projects that share rising to as high as 12% by 2028, with AI named as the primary driver of that growth.

The mechanism behind the demand surge is visible at the rack level. Blackwell-class systems require liquid cooling by design, and 120kW-class racks have ended air cooling's viability at the AI high end. That is not an incremental engineering change. It means new and retrofitted facilities must carry chilled-water or direct-liquid infrastructure before a single GPU is powered on, adding to both construction cost and grid draw before any compute work begins.

What this data does not cover is the supply side: whether grid operators can deliver the required capacity on the timelines AI builders need, or how interconnection queues are affecting deployment. It also gives only one efficiency reference point, Google's fleet-wide PUE of approximately 1.1, which represents a leading operator rather than an industry average. Readers should treat that figure as a ceiling on what is achievable rather than a description of what is typical.
